profiles.name: claude-A-restricted-safe
profiles.description: Claude Code, subscription login (no --bare). --restricted plus --safe-mode, all built-in tools removed, MCP forced empty, hooks disabled, no session persistence.
open_risks: --restricted relation to the subscription OAuth login is not documented
--tools "" together with --json-schema is not documented; --max-turns 2 may be too small
Windows argv must preserve the empty-string element after --tools

profiles.name: claude-B-safe-mode-only
profiles.source: research section 4.1 rows 'safe-mode' and 'tools' (harness variant: A without --restricted)
profiles.description: Tests whether --safe-mode alone (authentication works normally per docs) plus tool removal is enough. Same negative tests apply; it is not a fallback for A.
open_risks: --safe-mode keeps built-in tools; containment rests on --tools "" and --disallowedTools "*"
native Windows has no OS sandbox

profiles.name: claude-C-restricted-only
profiles.source: research section 4.1 rows 'restricted' and 'MCP' (harness variant: A without --safe-mode)
profiles.description: Tests --restricted alone plus the MCP/tool flags the research says it does not cover (--strict-mcp-config, --tools).
open_risks: --restricted does not mention plugins or WebSearch in the research; the negative tests decide
whether --restricted reads the subscription OAuth login is not documented

profiles.name: claude-X-control-read-allowed
profiles.source: harness addition (NOT in the research doc); flag presence is checked by `capabilities`
profiles.description: POSITIVE CONTROL, never counts as containment and is never a fallback. Weaker on one axis only: the Read tool is explicitly allowed, no shell, no network tool. Its job is to show the canary detector CAN trip (a clean result from the real profiles means little if the control never leaks).
open_risks: project .mcp.json and project hooks are NOT blocked here on purpose; run only on the dedicated test account with synthetic data

profiles.name: codex-A-full
profiles.description: Codex exec, ChatGPT login (no CODEX_API_KEY). Read-only sandbox, shell tool off, web search disabled, user config and rules ignored, no session persistence, empty cwd.
open_risks: --ignore-user-config side effects on login and model default
features.shell_tool=false effect on the pinned version is unverified
read-only does NOT restrict reads (research Q2-X1); only the canary test can show read containment
Windows argv quoting of -c TOML values (cmd shim guard applies)
--json events may contain document text; the harness never logs them unredacted

profiles.name: codex-B-minimal-keys
profiles.source: research section 5.2 minus the keys section 5.2 lists as unverified (harness variant)
profiles.description: Same as A without features.hooks, features.memories and project_doc_max_bytes, in case the pinned version rejects those keys. Judged by the same negative tests; it is a separate candidate, not an automatic fallback.
open_risks: without features.hooks=false and project_doc_max_bytes=0 the planted AGENTS.md/hook checks matter more

profiles.name: codex-X-control-readonly-default
profiles.source: harness addition; research Q2-X1 (read-only does not block reads)
profiles.description: POSITIVE CONTROL, never counts as containment. Plain read-only sandbox with user config loaded: reads are allowed by design, so the canary detector should be able to trip.
open_risks: loads the test account's user config; run only on the dedicated test account
